title: Certificates of Deposit: Establishing That an Interest Payout Account Has Been Closed
content:
On Piedmont Crescent Bank's Certificates of Deposit, the Interest Disposition says whether credited interest compounds or is paid out, and to which kind of account. This page states how the bank establishes that the account receiving paid-out interest has been closed.

## Rule

Only an Interest Disposition that pays interest out is tested: one paying to checking, or one paying to savings. An Interest Disposition of compounding names no receiving account, so there is nothing to test and nothing changes.

For an Interest Disposition that pays out, the bank takes the payout account named on the certificate and looks it up among the kind of account the Interest Disposition pays to: the owner's checking accounts where interest is paid to checking, the owner's savings accounts where interest is paid to savings. Only a status reading closed makes it a closed payout account; dormant, active or any other status leaves it open for this purpose.

## Input, judgement, outcome (hypothetical)

| Interest Disposition | Recorded payout account, as found in the matching kind of account | Closed? |
|---|---|---|
| Paid to checking | checking account, status closed | Yes |
| Paid to checking | checking account, status active | No |
| Paid to savings | savings account, status closed | Yes |
| Paid to savings | savings account, status dormant | No; only a closed status counts |
| Compounding | (none) | Not tested |
